title: Anurag Kashyap and Bobby Deol Made a Film About a Fading Star Accused of Rape. The Trailer Drops Wednesday.
excerpt: Inspired by real events and premiering at TIFF before its June 5 worldwide release, ‘Bandar’ brings together two of Bollywood’s most unpredictable forces.
body:
There’s a version of Bobby Deol’s career where he fades out quietly — another ’90s star who couldn’t adapt. Instead, he reinvented himself entirely. Animal turned him into a meme and a menace. Now, Bandar is about to turn him into something else: a serious actor in an Anurag Kashyap film.

The trailer drops on May 21.

The Story

Bandar (which translates to “Monkey” — the full international title is Monkey in a Cage) follows a fading television star who is accused of rape. It’s inspired by real events, though the makers haven’t specified which case. This is Kashyap territory — morally ambiguous, unflinching, more interested in making you uncomfortable than making you pick a side.

The screenplay is by Sudip Sharma and Abhishek Banerjee — the same writing team behind Paatal Lok, Kohrra, and Udta Punjab. If you’ve watched any of those, you know what to expect: layered characters, systemic rot, and dialogue that lands like a gut punch.

The Cast

Bobby Deol leads, and the ensemble around him is stacked. Sanya Malhotra (Dangal, Ludo), Saba Azad, Sapna Pabbi, Riddhi Sen (who won a National Award at 18 for Nagarkirtan), Raj B Shetty (the Kannada filmmaker-actor from Garuda Gamana Vrishabha Vahana), Jitendra Joshi (Constable Katekar from Sacred Games), and Nagesh Bhosle round out the cast.

This is not a vanity project. Kashyap has assembled performers known for disappearing into roles, not for selfies at airports.

The TIFF Factor

Bandar premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2025 — which tells you everything about the kind of film this is. TIFF isn’t Cannes (it’s more audience-friendly), but it’s where serious Indian cinema goes to find global validation. The film’s selection signals critical weight, and it means diaspora audiences in North America may have already been hearing the buzz.

For NRIs who follow Kashyap’s work — and there’s a loyal, vocal contingent from Gangs of Wasseypur days — Bandar arriving in theatres worldwide on June 5 is a significant event. This is the director’s first wide theatrical release in years, backed by Zee Studios with a full global rollout.

Bobby Deol’s Reinvention

Let’s talk about what Bobby Deol has pulled off. Five years ago, he was a punchline. The memes about his DJ career, the “Gupt” throwbacks, the endless comparisons to Sunny. Then Animal happened, and suddenly the internet realized that Bobby Deol playing a terrifying, silent antagonist was one of the most memorable villain performances in recent Bollywood history.

Bandar is the logical next step — a full lead role in a film that demands acting, not just screen presence. Early word from TIFF suggests Deol delivers. If true, this could be the performance that completes his second-act transformation.

What the Trailer Needs to Do

The teaser already set the tone: gritty visuals, emotional chaos, Bobby in a retro-rockstar avatar. The first song, “Kyun Mazaa Aa Raha Hai” by Vishal Mishra, hinted at a dangerous romantic undercurrent. The full trailer on May 21 needs to do one thing — convince audiences that this isn’t just another dark indie that’ll win awards and empty theatres. With Zee Studios’ marketing muscle and a June 5 release (a relatively open window), Bandar has a genuine shot at crossing over.

Produced by Nikhil Dwivedi’s Saffron Magicworks and backed by Zee Studios, Bandar releases worldwide on June 5, 2026. The trailer arrives May 21.
